answer: Continuous Work Thread. Each identity must publish a hash-linked chain of solved micro-tasks, and peers verify it against a shared mirror of prior outputs. Registration costs nothing, but sustaining many identities forces an attacker to split real compute across parallel chains. Because each thread must consume fresh timber—unique task inputs drawn from a scarce, rate-limited public pool—colluding identities exhaust their quota fast and stall. The concrete cost is sustained CPU-hours plus forfeited task rewards when chains fail cross-checks.
